newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares ease on uncertainty over Chidambaram.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares ease on uncertainty over Chidambaram.

text.p: Delhi share prices opened a shade lower on Tuesday as major investors stayed on the sidelines, awaiting former finance minister P. Chidambaram's party's decision on whether to join the government, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index was 1.10 points lower at 799.24 after 30 minutes of trade.
"The political conditions are not favourable for the capital market despite the formation of a new government," said Rakesh Anand of brokers Anand and Associates.
Chidambaram's Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC) on Sunday authorised its leader, G.K. Moopanar, to decide whether the regional party should join India's new government.

The TMC, part of the centre-left United Front coalition, decided on April 19 to stay out of the government after the alliance chose Inder Kumar Gujral instead of Moopanar as its leader and new prime minister.
Gujral has not appointed a finance minister in his cabinet, signalling the slot was open for Chidambaram.
TISCO shed 0.30 rupee to 183.00 in restricted trade, brokers said.
Larsen and Toubro lost 1.00 rupee to 225.45.
